subject.title: fix: deleting a session leaves its trajectory artifacts orphaned on disk

question: Should reset and delete preserve trajectory tool-call records under the same archive-retention policy as transcripts, including proven-owned files in `OPENCLAW_TRAJECTORY_DIR`?
rationale: The original deletion leak is a bug, but the expanded solution intentionally retains sensitive tool arguments and results across reset and deletion; code correctness alone cannot choose that forensic-retention boundary.

options.title: Match transcript retention
options.body: Archive proven-owned trajectory runtime and pointer files with the transcript suffix and reap them under the same configured retention rules.

options.title: Limit to delete cleanup
options.body: Fix user-initiated deletion orphaning without adopting reset-time forensic retention in this PR, leaving reset policy to the overlapping canonical discussion.

options.title: Delete trajectories immediately
options.body: Remove trajectory artifacts at lifecycle completion instead of retaining them, prioritizing data minimization over post-reset forensics.

recommendation.title: Match transcript retention
recommendation.body: Archive proven-owned trajectory runtime and pointer files with the transcript suffix and reap them under the same configured retention rules.

likelyOwner.reason: The PR is assigned to this reviewer, whose recent merged work spans trajectory cleanup and session lifecycle ownership.
